blocks.heading: Team Duties and Work Overview
paragraphs: I was a Software Consultant on Sparkhound's Web & Mobile team, working as a full-stack developer across both external client engagements and internal initiatives. The team developed and maintained custom web and mobile applications supporting business operations, workflow management, reporting, and data-driven processes.

My work primarily involved C#/.NET applications, JavaScript, SQL, Microsoft Azure, and Microsoft Power Platform. I worked across the full software development lifecycle, including requirements analysis, sprint planning, development, testing, deployment coordination, production support, and technical documentation.

Due to client confidentiality, application details are limited to high-level functionality. My projects included enterprise application modernization, workflow and reporting systems, database-backed applications, API integrations, and automation solutions.

blocks.heading: Individual Duties and Responsibilities
paragraphs: As a full-stack developer, I contributed to projects ranging from ongoing feature development to large-scale modernization efforts.

One major project involved modernizing legacy C#/.NET applications by upgrading them to supported LTS versions, updating dependencies, refactoring existing code, and making architectural improvements to improve maintainability.

I also contributed to decomposing a legacy 150-project C#/.NET solution into smaller, independently maintainable solutions. The initial effort focused on extracting business-orchestration components into a separate solution and establishing an independent build. I documented the architecture, dependencies, and build requirements so the modernization effort could continue after the development contract ended.

Another project involved developing new benefit-related reporting workflows. This work included creating database records, messaging events, brokers, and subscribers and validating the complete event-driven workflow through end-to-end testing. I also created technical documentation describing the workflow-development process to support future development and knowledge transfer.

I developed automated Microsoft licensing workflows using Power Automate and the PAX8 REST API to dynamically manage contractor licenses as staffing levels changed. I also developed PowerApps solutions that provided Excel-like data management, selective data refresh, and database persistence for business users.

Throughout these projects, I used GitHub Copilot and Claude as AI-assisted development tools for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. Generated output was reviewed and validated for correctness before being incorporated into the codebase.
I also used Azure DevOps for sprint tracking, work-item management, source control, and deployment coordination while collaborating with distributed development teams.

blocks.heading: Team Duties and Application Overview
paragraphs: I was a full-stack developer on a fully remote Agile team supporting internal and client-facing applications for enterprise clients including Walmart and McDonald's.
The applications were built using C#/.NET, JavaScript, HTML/CSS, and SQL, with development work organized through an Agile sprint process.

blocks.heading: Individual Duties and Responsibilities
paragraphs: I developed and enhanced application features based on stakeholder requirements, including administrative controls, report-generation improvements, and application maintenance functionality.

I added administrative controls to place the CRIMECAST system into maintenance mode without requiring individual account updates, and improved application organization by separating inline CSS and JavaScript into dedicated files.

I improved report generation by implementing queued long-running jobs and notifying users when reports were ready. I also supported the team's migration from TFS to Git-based repositories and improvements to development practices.

blocks.heading: Team Duties and Application Overview
paragraphs: I was a full-stack developer on a fully remote, geographically distributed team supporting the Global Print Web System microservices.

The application used JavaScript with Angular, HTML/CSS, Java, and SQL, with development focused on maintaining existing services, adding new functionality, and supporting migration toward cloud-based infrastructure.

blocks.heading: Individual Duties and Responsibilities
paragraphs: I maintained and modernized existing application features while developing new functionality using SOLID design principles. I also contributed to migration from traditional servers to cloud-based infrastructure supporting frontend hosting, backend databases, and device assignment.

I reworked device-assignment logic to eliminate hard-coded values and support future add-device requests, and led cleanup of obsolete and deleted printer records across device, model, and driver database tables.

I helped establish GitHub source-control and branch-protection practices and contributed to automated integration and end-to-end testing. I also created onboarding documentation covering local development and testing environment setup.

blocks.heading: Team Duties and Application Overview
paragraphs: I was a full-stack developer on a medical analytics platform within a Scrum-based Agile team, working across the frontend, backend APIs, and relational database.
The application used React, JavaScript, C#, .NET, Entity Framework, ASP.NET MVC, and SQL Server to provide analytics and data-driven functionality.

blocks.heading: Individual Duties and Responsibilities
paragraphs: I developed an alerts system across the application stack, including SQL tables, Entity Framework mappings, REST APIs, and frontend UI/UX for displaying and dismissing alerts.

I created APIs supporting dashboard data hydration and alerts-system interactions and streamlined SQL Server databases and relational schemas in preparation for future AWS data lake and machine-learning applications.

I collaborated with local and international development teams throughout application design and development and completed HIPAA compliance training, incorporating client data-security requirements into development and testing practices.

blocks.heading: Team Duties and Application Overview
paragraphs: I worked as a front-end web developer creating and maintaining custom client websites and supporting ongoing website development projects.

blocks.heading: Individual Duties and Responsibilities
paragraphs: I developed reusable website elements, updated existing functionality based on client requirements, and created and implemented hotfixes for the site's editor.
I collaborated with sales team members and server administrators to support client projects and resolve development issues.

blocks.heading: Project Information
paragraphs: This website was hand-written using HTML5, CSS3, PHP, and JavaScript. I own this domain and use Hostinger as my hosting platform.
The site is responsive and cross-browser friendly, and I added a custom script to clean copied text before it is pasted elsewhere.

I developed reusable PHP code blocks and JSON-based content structures to generate consistent project and work-experience sections from shared templates, reducing duplicated markup and simplifying future updates.
I use GitHub Copilot to improve site functionality, refine existing code, and identify opportunities to incorporate relevant technical keywords throughout the site's content.
The source code is managed in GitHub with automatic deployment hooks to Hostinger for fast publishing.

blocks.heading: Project Description
paragraphs: The goal of the project was to create a self-contained device that could record sound for survivors trapped under rubble during disaster response scenarios.
Our team used the ReSpeaker Core v2 and Python to process audio using a noise reduction pipeline before saving recordings to an SD card.
The device could run through a recording cycle, wait between intervals, and alert rescuers to potential survivor noise in the saved files.

blocks.heading: Project Description
paragraphs: This project was created for the Texas A&M Sailing Team to replace a paper-based inventory process with a digital system.
The backend was built using Ruby on Rails and the frontend used HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and PHP. We included admin/member roles, item tracking, and missing/broken item reporting.
The project emphasized agile sprint planning, behavior-driven testing, and user-access controls for team administrators.
